groups.label: Vowels & Consonants
rules: English has 5 vowel letters (A, E, I, O, U) representing 20 distinct vowel sounds.
Consonants can be voiced or unvoiced.

groups.label: Silent Letters
rules: Silent K in know, knee, knife.
Silent L in listen, talk, walk, half.
Silent W in write, answer, wrong.

groups.label: Diphthongs & Vowel Duration
groups.definition: Gliding vowel sounds and vowel length before voiced consonants
rules: Diphthongs move from one vowel sound to another within the same syllable (e.g. /eɪ/, /aɪ/, /əʊ/, /aʊ/).
Vowels are pronounced slightly longer before voiced consonants (e.g., bad /bæːd/) than before voiceless ones (e.g., bat /bæt/).

examples.m: Vowel shortening before voiceless /p/ vs lengthening before voiced /b/

groups.label: Consonant Clusters & Elision
groups.definition: Complex consonant combinations and sound dropping in natural speech
rules: Consonant clusters occur when two or three consonants appear together without intervening vowels (e.g., /str/, /kts/).
Elision involves dropping weak sounds (like /t/ or /d/) in rapid speech when flanked by other consonants.

examples.t: Next door ➔ /neks dɔːr/, Last night ➔ /lɑːs naɪt/
examples.m: Elision of final /t/ before another consonant
